title: candidate-feedback-draft-alicia-gomez-2026-03-06
content:
Candidate: Riley Park (applied: Senior Backend Engineer, Serving Runtime)
Interview date: 2026-03-03
Interviewers: Alicia Gomez (owner), Samir Patel, Ethan Hu
Interview format: 90m loop (30m system design, 30m coding, 20m behavioral + buffer)
---
Quick summary (top-line):
- Strong experience shipping low-latency backend systems (previously worked on request routing and scaling for real-time bidding platform).
- Good intuition around batching and queueing trade-offs for throughput vs latency.
- Coding was competent for the level but not exceptional — solved the problem with a clear approach but missed a couple micro-optimizations and edge-case tests.
- Communication is clear, pragmatic; asked good clarifying questions in system design.
- Some gaps on GPU/LLM-specific internals (KV cache layout, attention optimizations), but showed eagerness to learn and a reasonable mental model.

Notes by section:
System design (30m):
- Problem: design a high-throughput inference router that supports dynamic routing to model variants, prefix caching, and goals: 95th p95 latency <= 120ms for <128 tokens, autoscaling to handle traffic spikes.
- Riley proposed a layered architecture: frontdoor API (auth/rate limit) -> routing layer -> shardable workers with local KV cache + shared cache (redis-like) for cross-worker reuse.
- Liked: explicit mention of hybrid cache (local LRU + global Redis) and proactive cache warm-up for hot prefixes; thought about cache invalidation on model rollouts (stale prefix detection via model-versioned keys).
- Considerations: their approach relied on Redis for cross-worker KV which could add tail latency — Riley suggested async fallback and circuit-breakers, which is good. We discussed using Bloom filters to quickly check cache miss probability; they were familiar enough to propose it.
- Missed/weak: didn't consider token-level batching impacts when combining requests with different model variants (had basic idea to route by compatible variant but no concrete slotting/batching algorithm). Could probe more on how to preserve low p95 when batching across variants — maybe follow up with a deeper design question.

Coding (30m):
- Problem: implement a simplified in-memory rate limiter with token bucket semantics and an API to check/consume tokens per key. Edge cases: concurrent requests, clock skew, bursting behavior.
- Riley wrote a straightforward solution using per-key buckets + mutexes and an efficient refill calculation based on timestamps. Code ran in local whiteboard environment (pseudocode).
- Strengths: clean API, tested basic flow mentally, handled concurrency with locks.
- Weaknesses: didn't propose lock-free or sharding approach for high cardinality keys (we discussed using sharded maps or compare-and-swap); would likely need coaching to make it production-grade for high throughput. Also missed a minor bug around float math for refill and suggested integer-based tokens but didn't fully implement.

Behavioral / culture (20m):
- Riley is pragmatic, values shipping early and iterating. Provided examples of trade-offs made in prior job (latency vs cost).
- Good cross-functional instincts — mentioned working closely with infra and SRE teams on rollout automation and postmortems.
- Showed curiosity about Redwood's product modes (Dedicated/Private) and compliance constraints.

Scoring (1-5, 5=strong hire):
- System design / architecture: 4
- Algorithms & coding: 3
- Runtime & performance engineering (profiling, bottlenecks): 4
- LLM-specific infra knowledge: 2
- Communication & collaboration: 5
- Culture fit / ownership: 4
- Overall (composite impression): 4

Recommendation: Strong 'move forward' to hiring committee with the following caveats. Riley would be a solid hire for a role focused on building scalable routing/serving infra and would ramp into LLM-specific work. Not ideal as a pure researchers/ML infra person who must know quantization and attention kernels immediately. I recommend: move to take-home (or small workshop) focused on batching and cross-variant routing and a brief pairing session on KV cache strategies to validate their ability to design batching algorithms that preserve p95.

Suggested next steps / homework (for candidate):
- Take-home: design a batching strategy that groups incoming requests for low-latency models while maximizing throughput for high-latency variants; sketch data structures and scheduling heuristics. (1-2 days)
- Pairing: 60m session on prefix cache invalidation and rollout-safe cache keying (with Samir/Ethan).

Flags / concerns to raise to committee:
- LLM internals: low exposure to GPU execution, quantization, attention-level optimizations — will require mentoring from ML infra team if role needs that domain knowledge quickly.
- Production hardening: coding solution needs guidance for lock-free or sharded implementations for high-cardinality keys.

Compensation band / leveling (rough): Senior (IC3/IC4 equivalent) — target comp band consistent with senior backend infra hire.

Misc notes / questions for interviewers:
- Samir: please add notes on follow-up pairing outcomes once done.
- Ethan: add memory/space complexity notes on the token-bucket solution if you recall specifics from live coding.

Status: draft — waiting on Samir/Ethan additional inputs and the take-home prompt to be shared with candidate.
